critical_action_mapping_invalid.description: The Runtime host reports critical action mapping invalid.

critical_correlation_id_mismatch.description: The ledger reports critical correlation id mismatch.

critical_duplicate_event_id.description: The ledger reports critical duplicate event id.

critical_duplicate_event_type.description: The ledger reports critical duplicate event type.

critical_effect_disposition_mismatch.description: The ledger reports critical effect disposition mismatch.

critical_event_family_mismatch.description: The ledger reports critical event family mismatch.

critical_event_not_durable.description: The ledger reports critical event not durable.

critical_event_plan_invalid.description: The Runtime host reports critical event plan invalid.

critical_missing_action_id.description: The ledger reports critical missing action id.

critical_missing_correlation_id.description: The ledger reports critical missing correlation id.

critical_outcome_role_mismatch.description: The ledger reports critical outcome role mismatch.

critical_payload_action_mismatch.description: The ledger reports critical payload action mismatch.

critical_stable_link_mismatch.description: The ledger reports critical stable link mismatch.

critical_unsupported_intent.description: The ledger reports critical unsupported intent.

current_page_unknown.description: A code several owners emit with one meaning (contract-owned, A2a D3): current page unknown.

cursor_encode_failed.description: The MCP server could not encode a cursor.

cursor_invalid.description: An MCP cursor belongs to another query, Runtime connection or server process.

dangling_reference.description: A code several owners emit with one meaning (contract-owned, A2a D3): dangling reference.

database_maintenance_io_failed.description: The runtime database reports database maintenance io failed.

database_maintenance_sql_failed.description: The runtime database reports database maintenance sql failed.

debug_package_containment_failed.description: The Runtime host reports debug package containment failed.

debug_package_deadline_overflow.description: The Runtime host reports debug package deadline overflow.

debug_package_entry_count_overflow.description: The Runtime host reports debug package entry count overflow.

debug_package_instance_invalid.description: The Runtime host reports debug package instance invalid.

debug_package_name_invalid.description: The Runtime host reports debug package name invalid.

debug_package_path_not_absolute.description: The Runtime host reports debug package path not absolute.

debug_package_summary_invalid.description: The Runtime host reports debug package summary invalid.

debug_package_task_count_overflow.description: The Runtime host reports debug package task count overflow.

decision_candidate_not_selected.description: A dispatch decision record lists another candidate of the same instance (task_id) that was not selected.

decision_reason_missing.description: A decision that is not selected ended without a reason, which is a programming error in the evaluator. The candidate is still deferred and the evaluation round goes on, so the gap is visible rather than reported as none.
decision_reason_missing.common_causes: An evaluator path that defers or blocks a candidate without pushing its reason.
decision_reason_missing.handling: Report it with the evaluation's inputs; the evaluator path needs its reason.

decision_record.description: Scheduling decision reason: the policy state and the candidates a dispatch decision compared (decision record).

deferred_append_unconfirmed.description: The ledger reports deferred append unconfirmed.

deferred_replies_poisoned.description: The ledger reports deferred replies poisoned.

descriptor_mismatch.description: Catalog compile diagnostic: the scheduling documents of one catalog do not share one schema version and catalog descriptor.

destructive_state_mismatch.description: The scheduler refused a lease or queue operation: the lease's destructive step state does not match the request.

detect_failed.description: A recovery graph node's detection did not match.

detector_mismatch.description: An environment detection result has another detector identity.

device_battery_low.description: A handset is on no power source and its battery is below device_state.battery_min_percent (#398 R1 RD-5b, model-398 section 7.4): it is unavailable under device_state:battery_low. A handset plugged in never holds, charging or not. Recorded when a sample finds it; at a run's start the run does not start and no input is sent.
device_battery_low.common_causes: The cable is out or the charger is off.
device_battery_low.handling: Plug the handset in; the next sample lifts the hold.

device_binding_changed.description: actingctl devices bind or unbind: the state root's private binding file now binds the device of the handle to the handset alias, or no longer binds one to it; the change takes effect at the next start (Workflow #398 RD-1c).

device_binding_file_invalid.description: actingd refused the private binding file <state root>\private\device-bindings.json (#398 R1 RD-1b): it cannot be read, breaks its shape or schema, or binds an alias or a device twice. path names the file and device_binding_problem the rule. check-config and a start refuse before the ledger opens.
device_binding_file_invalid.common_causes: A hand edit of the private file, a file written by another release, or a file another program holds open.
device_binding_file_invalid.handling: Repair or remove the binding file and bind the devices again through the console or the CLI.

device_binding_missing.description: The private binding file <state root>\private\device-bindings.json binds no device to a handset instance (alias names it, #398 R1 RD-1b). check-config refuses at stage config_assemble; a start registers the instance unavailable and goes on.
device_binding_missing.common_causes: A handset instance added before its device was bound, or a binding removed.
device_binding_missing.handling: Bind a discovered device to the instance through the console or the CLI, then run actingd check-config again.

device_binding_unused.description: The private binding file binds an alias (alias names it) that no handset instance of the configuration has (#398 R1 RD-1b). check-config reports it as a note link of check_config_passed; nothing is refused.
device_binding_unused.common_causes: A handset instance renamed or removed while its binding stayed.
device_binding_unused.handling: Remove the stale binding, or add the handset instance it was meant for.

device_bindings_invalid.description: actingctl devices or an ac_device tool found the state root's private binding file (path) breaking its rules, or a binding would break them, as device_binding_problem says: for example the device is already bound to another alias. Nothing was written (Workflow #398 RD-1c).

device_bindings_write_failed.description: actingctl devices bind or unbind could not write the state root's private binding file (path); the failure is linked (Workflow #398 RD-1c).

device_config_invalid.description: An instance's device fields do not fit its device kind (#398 R1): for example a handset that names an endpoint, a serial or a discovery key, or selects a capture backend only emulators have, or an emulator that names scrcpy capture. alias names the instance and device_config_problem the rule. check-config refuses at stage config_assemble; a start refuses before the ledger opens.
device_config_invalid.common_causes: An emulator entry copied for a handset, or a backend chosen that the device kind does not have.
device_config_invalid.handling: Correct the instance as device_config_problem says. Fix the configuration and commit it again with acsetup --commit-config; run actingd check-config to confirm before restarting the daemon.

device_diagnostic_owner_mismatch.description: Event or record sanitization refused a value: device diagnostic owner mismatch.

device_error.description: A Lab error the contract's Lab error constructors name: device error.

device_handle_unknown.description: actingctl devices bind or ac_device_bind: adb does not list a device with this handle now; handles are the adb server's session numbers and change when a device is replugged or the server restarts (Workflow #398 RD-1c).

device_hold_lifted.description: A hold of a handset lifted (#398 R1 RD-5b, model-398 section 7.4): a sample found it cooled, plugged in, unlocked or no longer in use, or a run's start gate found it ready. With no hold left it is available again as its self-check and its link allow.

device_in_use.description: At a run's start another application than the instance's and the home screen's was in the handset's foreground, under device_state.in_use_gate (#398 R1 RD-5b, model-398 section 7.5): the run does not start and the handset is unavailable under device_state:in_use until a sample after device_state.in_use_backoff_ms finds no other application in front.
device_in_use.common_causes: A person is using the handset.
device_in_use.handling: Leave the handset on the home screen or the instance's application.

device_keyguard_dismiss_failed.description: A keyguard without a credential still showed on the handset after one wm dismiss-keyguard and the settle time. The run does not start.
device_keyguard_dismiss_failed.common_causes: The phone does not dismiss its keyguard from the shell.
device_keyguard_dismiss_failed.handling: Set device_state.keyguard_insecure to wait, or remove the keyguard on the phone.

device_kind_unsupported.description: actingctl devices bind or ac_device_bind: the alias is an instance of the selected configuration that is not a handset (device.kind handset); only a handset is bound to a device. actingd reports the same condition of a configuration as device_config_invalid (Workflow #398 RD-1c).

device_link_lost.description: A run, or a climbing recovery ladder, ended because the handset's wired device link left device (#398 R1 RD-2, model-398 section 4.4, 4.5): the device failure the run met is its caused_by link and no input follows. The default recovery_ladder.exclude_codes lists it: a cable is not something the ladder can fix.

device_link_reconnect_failed.description: The one adb reconnect of an offline handset's transport (device_link.offline_action = kick_once) failed (#398 R1 RD-2, model-398 section 4.3); the Runtime waits for the link as under wait. adb's text is the cause.

device_link_restored.description: A handset is back at device and the preparation queued after device_link.settle_ms passed (#398 R1 RD-2, model-398 section 4.3): it is available again and device.connected is true.

device_link_waiting.description: A handset left device (#398 R1 RD-2, model-398 section 4.2): its availability is withdrawn under device_link:<state>, device.link and device.connected are recorded, its retained session is closed and the Runtime waits for the link. Recorded once per state.

device_list_failed.description: actingctl devices or an ac_device tool could not read adb's device list: the install's adb (adb_path) did not start or ended with a failure, linked as foreign_os_error or foreign_adb_error with adb's text, bound device serials replaced by their labels (Workflow #398 RD-1c).

device_list_reported.description: actingctl devices list: the devices the install's adb lists now were printed, one row each with its handle, transport, state, model, the alias the state root's private binding file binds it to and a loopback endpoint, never a device serial, as ac_devices answers them (Workflow #398 RD-1c).

device_locked.description: A keyguard waits for a person on the handset: it asks for a credential (PIN, pattern, password or biometric), or it asks for none and device_state.keyguard_insecure is wait. The code covers "locked, and a person is needed", whether because of a secure lock or the wait policy. Nothing is sent; the Runtime never enters a credential.
device_locked.common_causes: The phone locked itself after its screen timeout.

device_path_invalid.description: A device_paths entry (nemu_folder, nemu_ipc_dll, droidcast_apk, minitouch_path or maatouch_path) is empty, not absolute, or names no existing file or folder. Nothing is opened. check-config refuses at stage config_assemble; a start refuses before the ledger opens.
device_path_invalid.common_causes: A relative path, a typing error, or a tool file that was moved, deleted or not installed.
device_path_invalid.handling: Point the entry at an existing absolute path, or remove it to use the default. Fix the configuration and commit it again with acsetup --commit-config; run actingd check-config to confirm before restarting the daemon.

device_screen_woken.description: The start gate of a run on a handset, or the check before an input, lit the screen with the wake key (#398 R1 RD-5b, model-398 section 7.3); the run goes on.

device_state_sampling_failed.description: The device-state sampling of the bound handsets could not start (#398 R1 RD-5b, model-398 section 7.2): its thread could not be spawned. The Runtime does not run without it.

device_state_unreadable.description: A device-state read of a handset (model-398 section 7.1) failed, or its answer has a shape the parser does not know; device_state_probe names the read. When adb answered, the foreign_adb_error link keeps adb's failure output or the answer that could not be read; when adb could not run or did not finish there is no link. The state is never guessed.
device_state_unreadable.common_causes: The phone left adb (unplugged, offline, unauthorized); the phone vendor prints another dumpsys format than the parser knows.
device_state_unreadable.handling: Check the device link; for an unknown shape, add a neutral sample of the new format to the parser.

device_thermal_hold.description: A handset's thermal status reached device_state.thermal_hold_at (#398 R1 RD-5b, model-398 section 7.4): it is unavailable under device_state:thermal until the status falls below device_state.thermal_resume_below. Recorded when a sample finds it; at a run's start the run does not start and no input is sent.
device_thermal_hold.common_causes: The handset grew hot during long runs or while charging.
device_thermal_hold.handling: Let the handset cool; the next sample below the resume level lifts the hold.

device_wake_failed.description: The handset's screen was still not awake after one KEYCODE_WAKEUP and the configured settle time (device_state.wake_settle_ms). The run does not start and no other input is sent.
device_wake_failed.common_causes: The settle time is shorter than the phone needs to turn the screen on; the wake key failed.
device_wake_failed.handling: Raise device_state.wake_settle_ms, or check the phone.

device_watch_failed.description: The device-link watch could not start, read an output of unknown shape, or ended more often within device_link.watch.restart_window_ms than device_link.watch.restart_limit allows (#398 R1 RD-2, model-398 section 4.3): every handset is unwatched and unavailable, emulators go on, and a person's self-check of a handset starts the watch again.

device_watch_restarted.description: The device-link watch, the Runtime's one adb track-devices process, ended and was started again within its restart budget (#398 R1 RD-2, model-398 section 4.3).

diagnostic_json_invalid.description: Ledger forensics reports diagnostic json invalid.

diagnostic_schema_unavailable.description: Ledger forensics reports diagnostic schema unavailable.

digest_cells_changed.description: Two failure frames differ because too many digest cells changed.

dispatch_instance_contended.description: A policy admission found the instance's admission guard taken by a keyless observe or probe for its whole short retry (about 100 ms). The dispatch intent already written is rejected at info; the candidate may run again from next_eligible_unix_ms, about one second later.
dispatch_instance_contended.common_causes: A read-only observation or a monitor probe of the instance was in progress when the dispatch was admitted.
dispatch_instance_contended.handling: Nothing to repair. The next policy evaluation dispatches the candidate once the observation has finished.

dispatch_instance_cooldown.description: A policy candidate met an instance whose takeover cooldown still runs after a previous owner ended without closing; the candidate is deferred with a wake at next_eligible_unix_ms, the cooldown's end. Nothing is written for it.
dispatch_instance_cooldown.common_causes: actingd was killed or crashed while it held a lease on the instance, and the new owner started less than the takeover cooldown (6 s by default) ago.
dispatch_instance_cooldown.handling: Nothing to repair. The candidate is evaluated again when the cooldown ends.

dispatch_instance_held.description: A policy candidate, or its admission, met an instance that a claim holds or that an eligible claim waits for (holder_kind names the holder, or the waiting claim that receives the key next; count is the number of eligible waiting claims). The candidate is deferred with no wake, or its intent is rejected at info; the policy driver evaluates again when a lease is released, transferred or expires.
dispatch_instance_held.common_causes: A stuck-recovery ladder, a startup package, an operator command or a direct task run holds the instance, or waits for it, when a dispatch is due.
dispatch_instance_held.handling: Nothing to repair. The candidate runs after the holder releases the instance; actingctl status shows lease_active and queued_request_count meanwhile.

dispatch_paused_global.description: An operator's global scheduling pause defers the dispatch.

dispatch_paused_instance.description: An operator's scheduling pause of the instance defers the dispatch.

dll_outside_root.description: The configured Nemu capture DLL lies outside the selected MuMu installation root. A MuMu resolution reason reaches outcomes where the refusing step runs: check-config's MuMu note (a note link of check_config_passed when the MuMu folder cannot be resolved), provider startup's device failure at a start, and the failure of a capture or input open in a running Runtime. The context the resolution recorded travels as optional values when the emitting path has it: count_kind, count and count_known (what was counted, how many, and whether the count is exact), install_source (which resolver rung chose the installation), configured_adb_class, explicit_root and explicit_dll (how the adb, the MuMu folder and the capture DLL were configured), and mumu_root.
dll_outside_root.common_causes: device_paths.nemu_ipc_dll pointing at a copied DLL or at another installation.
dll_outside_root.handling: Point device_paths.nemu_ipc_dll at the DLL inside the MuMu installation, or remove it to let the resolver find it.

dll_version_missing.description: No Nemu capture DLL carries the engine version (nx_device/<version>) of the adb or of the running MuMu executable, so the two cannot be paired. A MuMu resolution reason reaches outcomes where the refusing step runs: check-config's MuMu note (a note link of check_config_passed when the MuMu folder cannot be resolved), provider startup's device failure at a start, and the failure of a capture or input open in a running Runtime. The context the resolution recorded travels as optional values when the emitting path has it: count_kind, count and count_known (what was counted, how many, and whether the count is exact), install_source (which resolver rung chose the installation), configured_adb_class, explicit_root and explicit_dll (how the adb, the MuMu folder and the capture DLL were configured), and mumu_root.
dll_version_missing.common_causes: A capture DLL configured from outside the versioned engine folder, or an engine version whose DLL is missing.
dll_version_missing.handling: Configure the DLL of the engine version in use, or repair the MuMu installation.

document_too_large.description: A code several owners emit with one meaning (contract-owned, A2a D3): document too large.

drain_timeout.description: An install transition's drain did not finish before its deadline: the transition aborts and admission reopens on the old owner. The operation is install_transition; the status reports phase aborted with this failure code.
drain_timeout.common_causes: Work in flight that takes longer than the drain's timeout.
drain_timeout.handling: Wait until running work finishes, or begin the transition again with a longer timeout.

drive_package_invalid.description: A semantic drive package's navigation geometry is invalid.

drive_plan_invalid.description: A semantic drive plan input is invalid.

due_task_missing.description: The instance has no task due in this evaluation; its not-running row names the earliest wake (next_eligible_unix_ms) when one is known.
due_task_missing.common_causes: Every task of the instance ran or waits for its next occurrence.

duplicate_bundle_maintenance_role.description: Runtime contract validation refused a value: duplicate bundle maintenance role.

duplicate_bundle_pack.description: Runtime contract validation refused a value: duplicate bundle pack.

duplicate_capture_sequence_artifact_iden.description: Runtime contract validation refused a value: duplicate capture sequence artifact identity.

duplicate_emulator_capability_requiremen.description: The Runtime host reports duplicate emulator capability requirement.

duplicate_event_id.description: The ledger reports duplicate event id.

duplicate_frame_index.description: The artifact store reports duplicate frame index.

duplicate_id.description: A code several owners emit with one meaning (contract-owned, A2a D3): duplicate id.

duplicate_instance_alias.description: The Runtime host reports duplicate instance alias.

duplicate_instance_id.description: The Runtime host reports duplicate instance id.

duplicate_key.description: A code several owners emit with one meaning (contract-owned, A2a D3): duplicate key.

duplicate_runtime_instance_id.description: The Runtime host reports duplicate runtime instance id.

dynamic_target_not_evaluated.description: The page projection's reason for a blocked element or a missing target: dynamic target not evaluated.

earlier_target_failed.description: A page target was not evaluated because an earlier target of its page failed.

effect_evidence_insufficient.description: Forward projection evidence gap: a dispatched task's effects are only expected, inferred or not fully confident.

effect_incompatible.description: Catalog compile diagnostic: a task effect's direction or kind does not fit the pool it names.

effective_configuration_capture_evidence.description: Ledger forensics reports effective configuration capture evidence missing.

effective_configuration_fields_invalid.description: Ledger forensics reports effective configuration fields invalid.

effective_configuration_schema_unsupport.description: Ledger forensics reports effective configuration schema unsupported.

effective_configuration_source_links_mis.description: Ledger forensics reports effective configuration source links mismatch.

effective_configuration_source_missing.description: Ledger forensics reports effective configuration source missing.

effective_configuration_too_large.description: A code several owners emit with one meaning (contract-owned, A2a D3): effective configuration too large.

eligible_since_unknown.description: The Runtime host reports eligible since unknown.

empty_execution_backend_registry.description: The Runtime host reports empty execution backend registry.

empty_fact_observation.description: Event or record sanitization refused a value: empty fact observation.

emulator_autostart_failed.description: A configured start ended without its emulator started (Workflow #369 S6c): its failure is the caused_by link (a refused claim, a refused renewal, a failed control), recorded where it happened. A report line.

emulator_autostart_instance_unknown.description: A configured emulator start (actingd start_emulator, Workflow #369 S6c) names an alias that is not a registered instance; the Runtime host's start fails. alias names it.
emulator_autostart_instance_unknown.common_causes: A host configured by another embedder than actingd, whose own configuration check refuses such a start (start_emulator_requires_discovery_binding).
emulator_autostart_instance_unknown.handling: Correct the configured instances, then start again.

emulator_autostart_interrupted.description: A drain or a shutdown ended the autostart claim before its start; it releases its key, and the next daemon start enqueues it again (Workflow #369 S6c, H-5). A report line.

emulator_autostart_network_ready.description: An autostart claim read internet access from the operating system's connectivity status (Workflow #369 S6c, P3); elapsed_ms is how long it waited since its grant. The claim goes on to its start turn. A report line.

emulator_autostart_network_status_unknow.description: The operating system's connectivity status is unknown (connectivity_reason, and os_error when the system gave one); the autostart claim goes on without waiting (Workflow #369 S6c, P3). A report line.
emulator_autostart_network_status_unknow.common_causes: An older Windows without the connectivity query, a failed query, or a level the build does not know.

emulator_autostart_network_unready.description: No internet access was reported within 600 s (Workflow #369 S6c, P3): the configured start is refused with command.rejected and runtime.failed under the autostart claim, and the claim releases its key; elapsed_ms is the wait. Also its report line. The instance stays stopped.
emulator_autostart_network_unready.common_causes: The host had no network, or only local access, while actingd started.
emulator_autostart_network_unready.handling: Start the instance with emulator control once the network is up.

emulator_autostart_preparation_failed.description: A configured start was performed, but the connection preparation after it did not pass (Workflow #369 S6c); the preparation recorded its failure, and the ladder it admitted holds the key. A report line.

emulator_autostart_queued.description: actingd enqueued the autostart claims of the configured instances whose emulator is stopped (Workflow #369 S6c, model 369 H-5), after policy initialization and before runtime_ready. count is how many. A report line.

emulator_autostart_requires_physical_ins.description: A configured emulator start (Workflow #369 S6c) names a fixture instance, which has no emulator to start; the Runtime host's start fails. alias names it.
emulator_autostart_requires_physical_ins.common_causes: A host configured by another embedder than actingd, whose own configuration check refuses such a start.
emulator_autostart_requires_physical_ins.handling: Configure start_emulator only on a discovery-bound instance, then start again.

emulator_autostart_skipped.description: The instance already runs when its autostart claim holds the key (an operator started it): the claim ends without action (Workflow #369 S6c, H-5). A report line.

emulator_autostart_started.description: A configured start was performed and the connection preparation after it passed (Workflow #369 S6c); the key went to the instance's startup package, if one is configured. A report line.

emulator_autostart_superseded.description: An operator emulator control waits on the instance: the autostart claim releases its key before its start, with no failure pair (Workflow #369 S6c, H-5). A report line.

emulator_autostart_yielded.description: A scheduling pause holds the instance or the global gate: the autostart claim queues again as a gated entry and releases its key; the resume grants it again (Workflow #369 S6c, H-5). A report line.

emulator_capability_admission_refused.description: Provider startup refused the emulator capability profile built from MuMuManager discovery: the inventory or status read the Runtime needs is not available. mumu_manager_version is the version discovery reported and mumu_root the configured MuMu folder; the capability admission's refusal is the caused_by link. The start fails.
emulator_capability_admission_refused.common_causes: A MuMuManager release whose discovery report lacks a capability the Runtime requires.
emulator_capability_admission_refused.handling: Install a MuMu release the Runtime supports, then start again.

emulator_capability_probe_failed.description: The Runtime host reports emulator capability probe failed.

emulator_capability_unavailable.description: The Runtime host reports emulator capability unavailable.

emulator_control_adb_not_ready.description: The Runtime host reports emulator control adb not ready.

emulator_control_busy.description: The Runtime host reports emulator control busy.

emulator_control_endpoint_unresolved.description: The Runtime host reports emulator control endpoint unresolved.

emulator_control_failed.description: The Runtime host reports emulator control failed.

emulator_control_instance_unconfirmed.description: The Runtime host reports emulator control instance unconfirmed.

emulator_control_unavailable.description: Emulator control refused because the instance has no bound emulator control (fixture instance, explicit registration without discovery, or unregistered instance).

emulator_control_unsupported.description: Emulator control refused because the provider does not support the requested control.

emulator_control_wait_timeout.description: The Runtime host reports emulator control wait timeout.

emulator_restart_start_failed.description: An operator emulator restart whose Stop phase was confirmed and whose Start phase failed: the provider's launch failed or its readiness wait expired. The state read after the failure is applied (a stopped instance is pending, with device.connected false) and carried on the record, which is the request's one failure record and its receipt terminal. The control failure behind it (emulator_control_wait_timeout or emulator_control_failed) is the outcome's caused_by link (ledger revision 3); stop_result is left out when the host's stop-result table gives the stage no token.
emulator_restart_start_failed.common_causes: The instance did not boot within the start's readiness wait, or MuMuManager refused the launch.

emulator_restart_stop_failed.description: An operator emulator restart (a Stop phase and then a Start phase under one instance admission guard) whose Stop was not confirmed: the provider's shutdown failed (stop_result names the device stage) or its readiness wait expired (stop_result wait_timeout). After an expired wait the Start phase still runs (start_dispatched true); after any other Stop failure it does not. The restart fails whatever its Start did, and the record carries the last observed state; it is the request's one failure record and its receipt terminal, written after the Start phase when one ran. The control failure behind it (emulator_control_wait_timeout or emulator_control_failed) is the outcome's caused_by link (ledger revision 3); stop_result is left out when the host's stop-result table gives the stage no token.
emulator_restart_stop_failed.common_causes: The vendor's shutdown of the instance hung, for example its device process stayed after Android stopped (device_process_present true), or MuMuManager refused the shutdown.

emulator_stop_process_unverified.description: A Stop was confirmed by MuMuManager info alone: the process listing that checks that no vendor device process of the instance is left failed or passed its bound, so device_process_present is unknown. Recorded once per Stop under the request's links (a stuck-recovery ladder's on its emulator-restart rung), before command.validated.
emulator_stop_process_unverified.common_causes: The process listing (PowerShell) did not answer within its bound under host load, or could not start.

entry_missing.description: The watchdog's start found no Runtime entry program.

env_override_ignored.description: An ACTINGCOMMAND_* environment variable (variable names it) is set but not read, because allow_env_overrides is off. check-config reports it as a note link of check_config_passed; the start goes on without it.
env_override_ignored.common_causes: A variable left in the user's or the launcher's environment from earlier tests.
env_override_ignored.handling: Remove the variable, or set allow_env_overrides to true when the override is intended.

environment_value_expired.description: An environment detection result's value is older than its declared lifetime.

environment_value_low_confidence.description: An environment detection result's value has a confidence below the declared minimum.

errors_query_invalid.description: ac_diagnose could not form its errors view query.

event_fingerprinter_failed.description: The Runtime host reports event fingerprinter failed.

fact_adjustment_skipped.description: Workflow #384 D2-S3: a run confirmed an operation that declares a resource adjustment of fact_key, and the adjustment wrote nothing, for adjustment_reason. With after_read_missing (no reading of the key followed the confirmation) and amount_unresolved (the change the screen shows could not be read) the key's record is dropped, so the key is unknown until it is read again. task_id is the package's entry task. A task diagnostic row of the run, on its confirmation frame; the run itself succeeds.
fact_adjustment_skipped.common_causes: No reading mark of the key on a page the run passes after the operation, a mark or an amount that could not be read, a key with no current record, or an observation of the key already newer than the confirmation.
fact_adjustment_skipped.handling: Nothing to repair for base_missing, base_expired and newer_observation. For after_read_missing and amount_unresolved, check the package's marks and the amount's OCR target on the pages after the operation.

fact_adjustment_underflow.description: Workflow #384 D2-S3: a run's confirmed resource adjustment would take fact_key below zero: the change read on the confirmation frame is larger than the key's current value. Nothing is written and the key's record is dropped, so the key is unknown until it is read again. task_id is the package's entry task. A task diagnostic row of the run, on its confirmation frame; the run itself succeeds.
fact_adjustment_underflow.common_causes: The key's current record is stale or was misread, or the amount was misread.
fact_adjustment_underflow.handling: Check the key's reading mark and the amount's OCR target; the next reading of the key replaces the dropped record.

fact_reader_binding_ignored.description: Workflow #384 D2-S2: a Runtime start found an instance's recognition package binding invalid (its caused_by link is fact_reader_binding_invalid) and runs without it; the start goes on. Recorded as a note link of the recognition_packages row of config.subsystems.
fact_reader_binding_ignored.common_causes: The bound package could not be read at the start, or its marks are claimed by policy.facts or a ledger_fact pool.
fact_reader_binding_ignored.handling: Run check-config for the full refusal and fix the binding; until then the instance has no reader.

fact_reader_binding_invalid.description: Workflow #384 D2-S2: an instance's recognition maintenance package binding (instances[].recognition_package) is no reader: its package cannot be read (package_unreadable, caused by the loader's refusal), it does not qualify (designated_operation, no_marks, recognize_only, stability_termination), or one of its marks writes a key the configuration's policy.facts declares or a ledger_fact pool observes for the instance (policy_fact_authority, live_pool_key). check-config refuses the configuration; a Runtime start ignores the binding (fact_reader_binding_ignored).
fact_reader_binding_invalid.common_causes: acsetup or a hand edit bound a package that is not the standard package's recognition maintenance package, or the package changed.
fact_reader_binding_invalid.handling: Bind the standard package's recognition maintenance package, or fix the package or the configuration the reader_problem names.

fact_reader_document_mismatch.description: Workflow #384 D2: a reading mark is looser than the scheduling-layer selection document that reads its key (confidence_below_document) or the reading interval exceeds the freshness it needs (interval_exceeds_freshness). check-config warning; emitted once actingd loads a scheduling-layer document (D2-S1 decision D3) and, for the interval, once D2-S4 reads scheduling.fact_refresh.min_interval_ms.

fact_reader_missing.description: Workflow #384 D2-S2: the scheduler reads a realistic instance fact (resource.* or inventory.*; a catalog task's trigger or stop predicate in the instance's scope) that the instance's recognition maintenance package does not mark, or the instance has none. check-config warning; the configuration is still accepted.
fact_reader_missing.common_causes: The recognition maintenance package lacks a mark for the key, or no package is bound.
fact_reader_missing.handling: Add a mark for the key to the instance's recognition maintenance package, or bind one.

fact_reader_overdue.description: Workflow #384 D2-S5: the candidates of the instance have waited for the key (fact_key) for elapsed_ms, at least scheduling.fact_refresh.overdue_ms, without a usable reading. A transition of the fact refresh recorder, reported once per wait and only while a recognition maintenance package (package_id) serves the key; it reports only and never takes part in a decision. Not reported while overdue_ms is unset.
fact_reader_overdue.common_causes: The recognition maintenance package keeps failing or leaving the key unread, a limit holds it back, or the instance stays occupied; scheduling.fact_refresh.min_interval_ms is longer than the freshness the readers need.
fact_reader_overdue.handling: Look at the instance's fact_refresh rows (actingctl fact-refresh, ac_overview) for the reason and the gate, then fix the package, the limit or the occupation.

fact_record_invalid.description: The Runtime host reports fact record invalid.

fact_record_limit_exceeded.description: Event or record sanitization refused a value: fact record limit exceeded.

fact_refresh_exhausted.description: A limit (refresh_limit) holds back the instance's recognition maintenance package (package_id) that would read a key a candidate on the instance reads (fact_key): its daily limit is spent, its failed runs in a row reached the configured maximum today, the instance cannot place it, or the instance's activity window is closed or its activity budget spent (gate_code, the Runtime's admission code, when it gave one). The candidate is deferred until next_eligible_unix_ms when known.
fact_refresh_exhausted.common_causes: scheduling.fact_refresh.daily_limit or max_consecutive_failures is low for how often the instance's facts expire; the package keeps failing; the instance has no activity profile or is outside its activity windows.
fact_refresh_exhausted.handling: Raise the limit in scheduling.fact_refresh, fix the package's failures, or adjust the activity profile; the candidate is reconsidered when the limit's period ends.

fact_refresh_pending.description: A candidate on the instance waits for the instance's recognition maintenance package (package_id) to read a realistic key it read as unknown (fact_key, unknown_reason): the package is selected this round, or is held back for now by the gate gate_code (its minimum interval or failure backoff, an occupied, paused or unavailable instance, the host budget, a higher-ranked candidate, a Runtime admission gate), until next_eligible_unix_ms when known. failure_code is the code the package's latest run failed with, when it failed. The candidate is deferred, not failed.
fact_refresh_pending.common_causes: The instance fact is missing or out of date and the package is running now, or must wait for its interval, its failure backoff or its turn on the instance.
fact_refresh_pending.handling: None: the candidate is evaluated again when the reading lands, the gate lifts or the instance's key returns.

fact_refresh_requested.description: The instance's recognition maintenance package is requested to read a realistic instance fact key (fact_key) that a candidate on the instance read as unknown (unknown_reason; rule_id, the selection document rule that read it, when one did). One entry per key, on the package's own scheduling decision and on its dispatch's reason chain; the package competes with the instance's other candidates under the highest rank of the candidates it unlocks.
fact_refresh_requested.common_causes: The key was never read on the instance, or its record expired, went stale, lost confidence or has another type, and the instance's bound recognition maintenance package marks it.
fact_refresh_requested.handling: None: the package runs as an ordinary scheduled dispatch and its readings are published as instance facts; the candidates that read the key are scored in the round after the reading lands.

fact_refresh_resolved.description: Workflow #384 D2-S5: the candidates of the instance no longer wait for the key (fact_key) they waited for: the latest policy cycle found it known, or no candidate reads it any more. Only a transition of the fact refresh recorder (an actingd daemon line, and from AO-4 a policy.fact_refresh_transition record), never a decision reason; package_id names the instance's recognition maintenance package when one served the key.
fact_refresh_resolved.common_causes: The instance's recognition maintenance package or another run read the key, or the catalog changed.

fact_refresh_unbound.description: A scheduling-layer selection document read a realistic instance fact key (fact_key, a resource. or inventory. key that recognition writes) for a candidate on the instance, and the value is unknown (unknown_reason), but no reader can refresh it (reader_problem, when known). Only that candidate is deferred, with no wake; it is evaluated again when the instance facts, the catalog or the configuration change. Other candidates and instances are unaffected.
fact_refresh_unbound.common_causes: The instance has never had the fact read, or its record expired, went stale for the document, lost confidence or has another type; the instance has no recognition maintenance package bound, or that package does not mark the key.
fact_refresh_unbound.handling: Run a task that reads the fact on that instance, or bind a recognition maintenance package that marks the key; the candidate is reconsidered once the fact is published.

fact_refresh_unresolved.description: The instance's recognition maintenance package (package_id) ran successfully since the Runtime loaded the instance facts, and the key a candidate reads is still unknown because of it (fact_key, unknown_reason): the run gave no reading of the key (it did not reach the page that marks it, or the mark gave no reading), or the reading it gave had too little confidence or another type. The candidate is deferred until the package may run again (next_eligible_unix_ms).
fact_refresh_unresolved.common_causes: The package's route did not reach the marked page; the mark's region or OCR target does not match the screen; the recognition confidence is below the mark's floor or the document's.
fact_refresh_unresolved.handling: Check the package's reading marks and the task diagnostic's unresolved reading rows for the run; the package runs again after its minimum interval.

A missing or expired record never defers (there is no substitute value).
feature_locked.common_causes: A run met the feature's locked page earlier; a person or an agent marked the feature locked.
feature_locked.handling: Nothing to repair. Publish true for the key once the feature is unlocked; otherwise the task is tried again when the record expires.

fixture_backend_invalid.description: A fixture instance's fixture_backend breaks its rules: the alias is invalid, it lists no frame or too many, or max_inputs is above its bound. check-config refuses at stage config_assemble; a start refuses before the ledger opens.
fixture_backend_invalid.common_causes: An empty frame list or limits copied from another test setup.
fixture_backend_invalid.handling: Correct the fixture_backend members. Fix the configuration and commit it again with acsetup --commit-config; run actingd check-config to confirm before restarting the daemon.

fixture_backend_missing.description: An instance is treated as a fixture but has no fixture_backend member. check-config refuses at stage config_assemble; a start refuses before the ledger opens.
fixture_backend_missing.common_causes: A fixture instance whose fixture_backend was left out.
fixture_backend_missing.handling: Add the fixture_backend member, or make the instance a device instance. Fix the configuration and commit it again with acsetup --commit-config; run actingd check-config to confirm before restarting the daemon.

fixture_capture_outside_simulation_scope.description: The Runtime host reports fixture capture outside simulation scope.

fixture_device_fields_forbidden.description: A fixture (simulation) instance names a member only a device instance may have, such as application_id, an endpoint, a binding key, a backend or a timeout. check-config refuses at stage config_assemble; a start refuses before the ledger opens.
fixture_device_fields_forbidden.common_causes: A device instance turned into a fixture without removing its device members.
fixture_device_fields_forbidden.handling: Remove the device members from the fixture instance. Fix the configuration and commit it again with acsetup --commit-config; run actingd check-config to confirm before restarting the daemon.

fixture_execution_scope_forbidden.description: The Runtime host reports fixture execution scope forbidden.

fixture_frame_invalid.description: A fixture frame of a valid size cannot be built into a frame. check-config refuses at stage config_assemble; a start refuses before the ledger opens.
fixture_frame_invalid.common_causes: Pixel data that the frame builder refuses.
fixture_frame_invalid.handling: Regenerate the fixture frame. Fix the configuration and commit it again with acsetup --commit-config; run actingd check-config to confirm before restarting the daemon.

fixture_frame_size_invalid.description: A fixture frame's width and height give no valid RGB size, exceed the per-frame bound, or do not match the length of its pixel data. check-config refuses at stage config_assemble; a start refuses before the ledger opens.
fixture_frame_size_invalid.common_causes: A frame whose pixel data was cut or generated for another size.
fixture_frame_size_invalid.handling: Regenerate the frame with matching width, height and RGB data. Fix the configuration and commit it again with acsetup --commit-config; run actingd check-config to confirm before restarting the daemon.

fixture_monitor_scope_forbidden.description: The Runtime host reports fixture monitor scope forbidden.

fixture_resident_size_invalid.description: The fixture frames of one instance are larger together than the resident bound. check-config refuses at stage config_assemble; a start refuses before the ledger opens.
fixture_resident_size_invalid.common_causes: Too many or too large fixture frames for one instance.
fixture_resident_size_invalid.handling: Use fewer or smaller fixture frames. Fix the configuration and commit it again with acsetup --commit-config; run actingd check-config to confirm before restarting the daemon.

frame_retention_counter_failed.description: A frame moved into its kept folder, but the move counter kept/.moves (entry) could not be written, so other processes may find moved frames only at their next walk of the kept folders, within 60 s. Reported once per process.
frame_retention_counter_failed.common_causes: A folder or a read-only file where kept/.moves should be; access to the kept folder denied.
frame_retention_counter_failed.handling: Remove whatever occupies kept/.moves so that a file can be written there; the next move writes the counter again.

frame_retention_move_failed.description: The frame cleaner could not move an error or Lab frame into its kept folder (entry, relative to the state root) for another reason than a held or absent file; the frame stays at its object key, is not tried again by this process, and is tried again after a restart.
frame_retention_move_failed.common_causes: A file where the kept date folder or leaf should be; access to the state root's kept folder denied; a full disk.
frame_retention_move_failed.handling: Remove whatever blocks the kept folder named by entry, then restart actingd so that the cleaner tries again.

frame_retention_remove_failed.description: The frame cleaner could not delete a due frame at its object key for another reason than a held or absent file. The frame stays, is not tried again by this process, and is tried again after a restart.
frame_retention_remove_failed.common_causes: Access to the state root's artifacts folder denied by the file system or by security software.
frame_retention_remove_failed.handling: Check the file's permissions and any program that blocks it, then restart actingd so that the cleaner tries again.
