pack_admission_lifted.description: A task package suspension was lifted because the package's content hash (actual_digest, as measured now) changed; a Runtime build that differs starts without the suspension. The next preparation tries the package once; the same refusal under the same content hash and build suspends it again. runtime_commit is absent for a build without a known commit. Copied once per instance the suspension was copied for, as a goal_missed planning signal.
pack_admission_lifted.common_causes: The package was replaced or the Runtime upgraded.

pack_admission_suspended.description: A task package was suspended because admission refused it with a code of scheduling.pack_admission.suspend_codes (failure_code) under the Runtime build runtime_commit (absent for a build without a known commit); actual_digest is the package's content hash measured right after the refusal (absent when it could not be measured, M-PKG D18). Every task bound to the package, on every instance, is deferred with this code and never prepared again until the content hash or the build changes. Other task packages of the same standard package are unaffected; a standard package is never suspended as a whole. The evaluation copies it once per instance it defers as a goal_missed planning signal (Workflow #386 SR-3); check-config lists it as a note.
pack_admission_suspended.common_causes: A package that needs more sampling time than its timeouts allow (recognition_sample_budget_invalid), typically after a Runtime upgrade with an unchanged package.
pack_admission_suspended.handling: Fix and replace the package; the suspension lifts when its content hash changes. A Runtime build that accepts it lifts it too.

pack_registry_dispatch_withdrawn.description: An unload withdrew a dispatch of the package that was admitted but had not started; recorded in the evaluation record and the reason chain.
pack_registry_dispatch_withdrawn.common_causes: The package was unloaded while one of its dispatches waited to start.

pack_registry_entry_invalid.description: LoadPack replacing a start-table entry gave another run mode than the entry it replaces (scheduled_execution present on one side only, or another mode); the table is unchanged.
pack_registry_entry_invalid.common_causes: The replacing binding left out or changed scheduled_execution.
pack_registry_entry_invalid.handling: Give the replacing binding the entry's run mode. To change a run mode, change the configuration and restart the Runtime.

pack_registry_entry_unknown.description: LoadPack restoring a start-table entry, or UnloadPack, named a package that is neither in the effective loaded-pack table nor in the configuration; the table is unchanged.
pack_registry_entry_unknown.common_causes: A mistyped package id; a package that the configuration does not bind.
pack_registry_entry_unknown.handling: Use a package id that the configuration binds or that a LoadPack in this Runtime epoch loaded.

pack_registry_loaded.description: LoadPack succeeded (#389 U-3): the package, structurally admitted from its location, is in the Runtime's in-memory loaded-pack table, either restored from the start table or as a new or replacing binding. The change lasts until the Runtime restarts.
pack_registry_loaded.common_causes: A Lab debugging session loaded a package.

pack_registry_not_loaded.description: One of the Runtime's own requesters met a package that is not loaded: a policy candidate is deferred (before SR-11's pack_schedule_closed), a startup package or a ladder rung that needs it is skipped, a fact reader's dispatch is deferred, or a queued startup-package claim is dropped by an unload.
pack_registry_not_loaded.common_causes: The package was unloaded with UnloadPack in this Runtime epoch.
pack_registry_not_loaded.handling: Load the package again with LoadPack, or restart the Runtime to return to the configuration's packages.

pack_registry_unloaded.description: UnloadPack completed (#389 U-3): the package left the in-memory loaded-pack table. Runs that used it were stopped through the same path as a run stop (scheduled runs, startup and ladder packages, prerequisite layers, and manual runs of the same package_id), its admitted but unstarted dispatches were withdrawn and its queued startup-package claims dropped. The result lists the stopped runs by request id and the withdrawn dispatches, and marks the runs still stopping when the wait ended. The change lasts until the Runtime restarts.
pack_registry_unloaded.common_causes: A Lab debugging session unloaded a package.
pack_registry_unloaded.handling: Nothing to repair. A restart loads the configuration's packages again.

pack_schedule_closed.description: Every candidate of the task package package_id is deferred because the pack schedule that applies to the instance (an instruction row of session.pack.schedule, else a default row of the standard package) says the package is not schedulable now; next_eligible_unix_ms is the end of the covering row.
pack_schedule_closed.common_causes: A person or an agent closed the package for a period; the standard package closes it by default.
pack_schedule_closed.handling: Nothing to repair. Write a row that makes the package schedulable, or wait for the row to end.

pack_schedule_unknown_package.description: A session.pack.schedule row names a package that no task of the active catalog uses. Reported once per evaluation cycle; the row is kept and has no effect until a catalog uses the package. Not an error.
pack_schedule_unknown_package.common_causes: A row written for a package of another standard package or catalog generation.
pack_schedule_unknown_package.handling: Nothing to repair; remove the row if it is no longer wanted.

perf_baseline_clamped.description: A learned baseline of the shadow measurement is held at its clamp around the configured initial value (baseline_us, held at limit_us), for the host or one instance (instance_id). The status read (PerformanceStatus) carries it while the baseline stays held (Workflow #385 PERF sections 3.5 and 11, P-m).
perf_baseline_clamped.common_causes: The configured initial baseline of the signal is far from what the host or the backend really takes.
perf_baseline_clamped.handling: Look at the calm values and set performance.responsiveness initial_baseline_us of that signal (per backend) nearer to them, or widen baseline.clamp_min_milli or clamp_max_milli.

perf_config_invalid.description: The performance section breaks a rule at start or in check-config (Workflow #385 P-c, PERF section 11): a curve that does not fall from 10000 to 0, a factor or share outside its range or moving the wrong way, a stage stepping back, a full share dropping straight to none, calibration tolerances not rising, a stage boundary inverted, a pressure-only stage beyond S2, or another rule of the section; config_key names the key and config_value_problem the rule. The start is refused before the ledger opens.
perf_config_invalid.common_causes: A hand-edited performance key whose value breaks the section's rules.
perf_config_invalid.handling: Fix the key named by config_key, commit the configuration again and restart.

perf_hold_expired.description: A policy run was held at its pace checkpoint longer than the hold limit (timeout_ms) and ended; its cancellation reason is PerformanceYield, it is owed a rerun, and the recovery ladder may start once performance releases the instance (Workflow #385 PERF §7.4, M387 §3.7). Registered by SH-1; P-h emits it.
perf_hold_expired.common_causes: The host stayed in the deepest pacing stage longer than the hold limit.
perf_hold_expired.handling: Nothing to repair for one occurrence; the run is rerun.

perf_probe_unavailable.description: A host probe of the shadow measurement could not run (its thread could not start, or it failed); its signal stays unknown and every other signal goes on. The status read (PerformanceStatus) carries it, caused by the failure (Workflow #385 PERF sections 3.2 and 11, P-m).
perf_probe_unavailable.common_causes: The operating system refused a thread, or the probe's clock or lock failed.
perf_probe_unavailable.handling: Restart actingd; if it recurs, check the host's resources. Pacing without the probe reads the remaining signals.

perf_run_yielded.description: Performance pacing ended a policy run to be rerun: it reached its wall-clock ceiling after pacing lengthened it (yield_cause wall_ceiling) or was preempted while held (preempted). Its cancellation reason is PerformanceYield; the run settles as a condition termination and is owed a rerun (Workflow #385 PERF §7.4). Registered by SH-1; P-k and P-h emit it.
perf_run_yielded.common_causes: The host stayed slow long enough for a lengthened run to reach its ceiling, or the instance was paused by its share while the run was held.
perf_run_yielded.handling: Nothing to repair for one occurrence; the run is rerun.

perf_stage_changed.description: The shadow measurement's stage of the host (no instance_id) or of one instance changed: the curve read at the tracked responsiveness, with a pressure's stage-one floor. perf.pacing_changed carries it; under mode observe nothing takes effect (Workflow #385 PERF sections 4 and 12.1, P-m).
perf_stage_changed.common_causes: The host's probes or an instance's frame acquisitions and touch responses slowed down or recovered, or a pressure began or ended.
perf_stage_changed.handling: Nothing to repair: it is a measurement. Read the views with actingctl perf-status or the performance block of ac_overview.

policy_monitor_config_invalid.handling: Set the policy.monitor values within their ranges, or remove them for the defaults. Fix the configuration and commit it again with acsetup --commit-config; run actingd check-config to confirm before restarting the daemon.

policy_monitor_request_retried.common_causes: The host is overloaded (CPU near 100 %) or the Runtime's ledger writer stalls longer than the monitor's I/O timeout.
policy_monitor_request_retried.handling: None while the failures stay under the limit. If it recurs, lower the host load or raise policy.monitor.io_timeout_ms.

policy_monitor_retries_exhausted.description: actingd's policy monitor gave up: after limit_count retries in a row (policy.monitor.retry_limit), one more request to its own Runtime got no receipt header in time. actingd then stops with that request's failure.
policy_monitor_retries_exhausted.common_causes: The Runtime did not answer its local IPC for longer than the retries cover: a sustained host overload, or a Runtime that hangs.
policy_monitor_retries_exhausted.handling: Check the host load and the Runtime's ledger writer, then start the Runtime again. If the host is expected to stall this long, raise policy.monitor.retry_limit, retry_backoff_max_ms or io_timeout_ms.

policy_rerun_exhausted.common_causes: A package's time declarations are too tight even at stage s0.
policy_rerun_exhausted.handling: Look at the package's timeouts, sampling and entry-cost declarations.

policy_rerun_expired.description: An owed rerun was not served before its bookkeeping window ended (window_end_unix_ms, taken from the settlement record). The run's failure then counts as an ordinary failure; the missed round is not carried into the next day.
policy_rerun_expired.common_causes: The condition (load or a blackout) lasted until the window ended.
policy_rerun_expired.handling: Nothing to repair for one occurrence. If it repeats, look at host load or the blackout table.

policy_rerun_owed.description: A rerun of a condition-terminated policy run (failure_code; count is its consecutive condition termination in this occurrence) is owed: the evaluator treats the pair as triggered and past its cooldown and promotes it ahead of the instance's other candidates. It is an ordinary policy dispatch in the instance's one queue.
policy_rerun_owed.common_causes: The previous run ended with a condition code (time too short, sampling timeout, blackout stop, performance yield or hold, entry-cost time check) and the condition has lifted.

policy_rerun_waiting.description: An owed rerun waits because the instance's pacing stage (pacing_stage) is above scheduling.rerun.resume_stage, or fell to it less than resume_settle_ms ago. It is evaluated again when the stage changes.
policy_rerun_waiting.common_causes: Host load keeps the instance at stage s3 or s4.
policy_rerun_waiting.handling: Nothing to repair; the rerun follows when the stage settles at or below the resume stage, or expires at the end of its bookkeeping window.

policy_settlement_dispatch_left_open.description: After a start's reconciliation, a scheduled dispatch (its task's procedure is one the policy driver runs as a scheduled run) still has no outcome. The start settles every scheduled dispatch it can; this one stays open, and a later dispatch on its instance may be refused as a conflict. Recorded once per start, under the run's links, which carry the run id; lease_id is present when the dispatch has one lease grant.
policy_settlement_dispatch_left_open.common_causes: The run's instance is no longer in the configuration, or the run's lease ended in more than one way (for example two transfers).
policy_settlement_dispatch_left_open.handling: Report it with the run id: the open dispatch needs a fix in the Runtime. When the instance was removed from the configuration, adding it back lets the next start settle the run.

policy_settlement_dispatch_unsettled.description: A start could not settle a scheduled run: the host's recovery or the ledger refused its settlement (failure_code is the refusal's code). The start carries on: the run's dispatch stays open, out of the active workloads, and the run's instance is paused with this code as the pause reason, so no new dispatch meets the open one. Recorded once per start, under the run's links, which carry the run id; lease_id is present when the dispatch has one lease grant.
policy_settlement_dispatch_unsettled.common_causes: A run whose recorded facts do not fit any settlement the Runtime knows, for example a ledger written by a defect in an earlier version.
policy_settlement_dispatch_unsettled.handling: Report it with the run id and failure_code: the open dispatch needs a fix in the Runtime. After looking, lift the instance's scheduling pause (resume scheduling for the instance) to let other tasks dispatch there again; the open dispatch itself stays open until a version that can settle it starts.

policy_settlement_release_recovered.description: A start found a scheduled run whose dispatch has no outcome and whose lease has no lease.released under its run links, wrote the missing release (effect not_performed) and settles the run once: from its terminal when it has one, otherwise as interrupted (policy_settlement_interrupted), so the dispatch is closed; the first such interruption of its pair in a row is lifted by the same start. Recorded once, under the run's links, which carry the run id.
policy_settlement_release_recovered.common_causes: The Runtime ended between a run's task terminal and its lease end (for example inside a failed run's hand-off to its stuck-recovery ladder), in the middle of a run (a reboot or a killed process), or after a scheduled dispatch's lease grant and before its run's first task event.
policy_settlement_release_recovered.handling: Nothing to repair: the run counts as its terminal says, or as interrupted when it has none. A second interruption of the same pair in a row keeps the pair paused until its package changes, as for any interrupted settlement.

port_conflict.common_causes: A port kept from an explicit entry, or a MuMu instance whose port changed.
port_conflict.handling: Remove port from the discovery-bound instance (discovery supplies it) or set it to the discovered port. Fix the configuration and commit it again with acsetup --commit-config; run actingd check-config to confirm before restarting the daemon.

port_unverifiable.common_causes: A port declared for an instance that was not running at the start.
port_unverifiable.handling: Remove port from the discovery-bound instance (it is then bound pending until started), or start the instance first.

provider_native_failed.description: Provider startup failed in the device layer with a failure that names no registered code of its own (no MuMu resolution reason): device_category names the device failure's category when it has one and mumu_root the configured MuMu folder; the device's own text is a foreign_other_error link. check-config reports the same outcome as a note when the MuMu folder cannot be resolved.
provider_native_failed.common_causes: MuMuManager failing or timing out, an unreadable MuMu folder, or an OS error during discovery.
provider_native_failed.handling: Check that MuMu is installed and MuMuManager runs, set mumu_root when MuMu is not found, then start again; report it when it repeats.

provider_startup_failed.description: The diagnostic code of a ledger diagnostic record: provider startup failed.

provider_version_below_minimum.description: The version MuMuManager reports is below the Runtime's minimum supported version (a Runtime policy floor, not a vendor minimum). A MuMu resolution reason reaches outcomes where the refusing step runs: check-config's MuMu note (a note link of check_config_passed when the MuMu folder cannot be resolved), provider startup's device failure at a start, and the failure of a capture or input open in a running Runtime. The context the resolution recorded travels as optional values when the emitting path has it: count_kind, count and count_known (what was counted, how many, and whether the count is exact), install_source (which resolver rung chose the installation), configured_adb_class, explicit_root and explicit_dll (how the adb, the MuMu folder and the capture DLL were configured), and mumu_root.
provider_version_below_minimum.handling: Update MuMu to a supported release.

provider_version_unparseable.description: MuMuManager's version answer is not a four-part numeric version. A MuMu resolution reason reaches outcomes where the refusing step runs: check-config's MuMu note (a note link of check_config_passed when the MuMu folder cannot be resolved), provider startup's device failure at a start, and the failure of a capture or input open in a running Runtime. The context the resolution recorded travels as optional values when the emitting path has it: count_kind, count and count_known (what was counted, how many, and whether the count is exact), install_source (which resolver rung chose the installation), configured_adb_class, explicit_root and explicit_dll (how the adb, the MuMu folder and the capture DLL were configured), and mumu_root.
provider_version_unparseable.common_causes: A MuMu release whose version output changed, or a damaged MuMuManager answer.
provider_version_unparseable.handling: Update MuMu to a supported release; report the version text if it repeats.

recognition_pack_undeclared.description: Workflow #384 D2-S2 (transitional warning): a pack of a bundle generated with maintenance declarations only navigates and reads (it qualifies as a recognition maintenance package) but the declarations do not name it for recognition. The resource repositories make it an error once their recognition packages are declared (D2-S6).
recognition_pack_undeclared.common_causes: A reading pack of the standard package is not declared in maintenance.json.
recognition_pack_undeclared.handling: Declare the standard package's one recognition maintenance package with the use recognition, and merge other reading packs into it.

recognition_regression_evidence_invalid.description: An --evidence file of actinglab recognition-regression is not one page of a run's evidence as actingctl run evidence or ac_run_evidence answer it (request_id, and steps with step_index and frames[].ref), within 16 MiB; or two pages are of different runs; or the pages name no frame.
recognition_regression_evidence_invalid.common_causes: The answer was edited or truncated, pages of two runs were given, or the run kept no frame.
recognition_regression_evidence_invalid.handling: Save the run's evidence pages unchanged, all of one run, and name a run whose frames were kept.

recognition_regression_evidence_unreadab.description: actinglab recognition-regression could not open or read an --evidence file.
recognition_regression_evidence_unreadab.common_causes: The path does not exist or is not readable.
recognition_regression_evidence_unreadab.handling: Name a readable file: the saved answer of actingctl run evidence or ac_run_evidence.

recognition_regression_frame_invalid.description: A frame that the evidence of actinglab recognition-regression references is not a PNG image, or its material does not read for another reason than its absence, or its PNG does not decode. Nothing was compared. A frame whose material is gone is not this error: it is listed as material_missing.
recognition_regression_frame_invalid.common_causes: The frame's material was replaced or damaged.
recognition_regression_frame_invalid.handling: Check the state root's artifact store; replay another run.

recognition_regression_frame_unknown.description: A frame reference of the --evidence of actinglab recognition-regression names no verified capture frame of the run in the ledger of --state-root. Nothing was compared.
recognition_regression_frame_unknown.common_causes: The evidence was read from another Runtime than --state-root names, or was edited.
recognition_regression_frame_unknown.handling: Read the evidence from the Runtime whose state root is given, and save it unchanged.

recognition_regression_ledger_unreadable.description: actinglab recognition-regression could not read the ledger of --state-root: it does not open, it is incomplete or corrupt, an artifact does not verify, or the run's events cannot be read. Nothing was compared.
recognition_regression_ledger_unreadable.common_causes: The path is not a Runtime state root, or its ledger is damaged.
recognition_regression_ledger_unreadable.handling: Name the state root of the Runtime that recorded the run; run the ledger checks if it is damaged.

recognition_sample_budget_insufficient.description: A running task had less time left (remaining_ms) than the next page recognition needs (required_ms), so it ended before sampling. Only for a run in progress; at admission the same condition is recognition_sample_budget_invalid. A scheduled run that ends with it settles as a condition termination and is rerun. Not a recovery ladder trigger.
recognition_sample_budget_insufficient.common_causes: Slow steps or long waits earlier in the run used up the task time; host load lengthened the run.
recognition_sample_budget_insufficient.handling: Nothing to repair for one occurrence; the rerun follows. Repeated occurrences at stage s0 mean the task timeout is too tight for its declared sampling.

recognition_sample_budget_invalid.description: Admission refused a task package whose declared sampling needs more time (required_ms) than the smaller of its step and task timeouts (limit_ms); pack_operation_id names the operation when one operation exceeds it. It is a suspend code by default: the Runtime suspends the task package until its content or the Runtime build changes (contracts/policy-suspension.md). Not a recovery ladder trigger.
recognition_sample_budget_invalid.common_causes: A package written for an older kernel whose budget rule was looser; a package whose consensus or candidate sampling declarations outgrew its timeouts.
recognition_sample_budget_invalid.handling: Raise the package's step or task timeout, or reduce its declared sampling, and replace the package; the suspension lifts when its content hash changes.

recognition_sample_deadline_exceeded.description: A recognition observation (capture, multi-frame sampling and recognition) did not finish within its window, and every observe-only retry (attempts: the configured base plus the pacing curve's extra retries) ran out too; stage names the observation. A retry never repeats an input. A scheduled run that ends with it settles as a condition termination and is rerun after the condition lifts (contracts/policy-suspension.md). Not a recovery ladder trigger.
recognition_sample_deadline_exceeded.common_causes: A slow or stalled emulator under host load; a page whose consensus needs more frames than its window allows at the current pacing.
recognition_sample_deadline_exceeded.handling: Nothing to repair for one occurrence; the rerun follows. Repeated occurrences at stage s0 mean the package's sampling or timeouts are too tight.

recognition_sample_deadline_or_permissio.description: Retired (Workflow #386 SR-1). Recognition sampling ran past its deadline, or the runtime's sampling checkpoint answered that sampling may not go on. A running task never loses its permission while it holds its lease, and the checkpoint now only reports a cancellation under the cancellation's own code (contained_task_deadline_exceeded, contained_task_cancelled, contained_task_paused); a sampling deadline is recognition_sample_deadline_exceeded, after the observation's observe-only retries.
recognition_sample_deadline_or_permissio.common_causes: A slow sampling under host load; never a lost permission.
recognition_sample_deadline_or_permissio.handling: None in 0.12.0 and later: the code is no longer emitted.

recognition_sample_geometry_changed.description: The frame geometry changed between recognition samples.

recognition_samples_unavailable.description: The recognition samples a target's consensus needs are unavailable.

recognition_sampling_runtime_unsupported.description: The runtime cannot take the recognition samples a target's consensus needs.

record_click_follow_invalid.description: Workflow #396 REC-4: a click of a Lab recording step that follows a template mark (record mark --click-follow, a request's click.follow) does not hold; mark_id is the followed mark and follow_problem says why. A declaration that cannot hold (not_template, not_required, guard_conflict) refuses record mark with this code (exit 3) and nothing is written. A frame of the step on which the click does not hold (primary_mismatch on the primary frame, template_unmatched or click_outside_frame on any live frame) is a refused mark's reason inside record_mark_rejected, with the frame. The stage is record_click_follow_check.
record_click_follow_invalid.common_causes: The click follows a color, OCR or check mark, a template that only an any_of check names, or another guard was named; the template matches elsewhere on the primary frame, is not found on a sample frame, or the followed click box leaves a sample frame.
record_click_follow_invalid.handling: Follow a required template mark of the step and let it be the guard; crop the template so that its best match on the primary frame is the crop itself; give it a search area that covers every position it moves to, and a click box that stays inside the frame there.

recovery_ladder_code_unclassified.description: The recovery ladder met a code the embedded catalog does not list and read it as ladder class none (raw_code is its spelling); recorded once per process and code. No trigger item matches it by class.
recovery_ladder_code_unclassified.common_causes: A code a newer component emits that this build's catalog does not list yet.
recovery_ladder_code_unclassified.handling: Update the Runtime; to start a ladder on the code, list it in a trigger item's codes once the catalog has it.

recovery_ladder_config_invalid.description: The recovery_ladder section breaks a rule of its whole-section check (config_key names the key, config_value_problem the rule); startup and check-config refuse the configuration. The same values sent by a ConfigureSettings instruction are refused as config_value_invalid with the same key and problem, and the Runtime keeps its configuration.
recovery_ladder_config_invalid.common_causes: Two trigger items with one id, a stage no item may name, a code or class the catalog does not list, count and window_ms on the wrong item, a start rung beyond the rungs, a rung bound below the device layer's, or a claim TTL or bound beyond the longest renewal.
recovery_ladder_config_invalid.handling: Fix the key config_key names as config_value_problem says, then commit the configuration again.

recovery_ladder_continuation_granted_ear.description: The Runtime host reports recovery ladder continuation granted early.

recovery_ladder_drain_requested.description: A stuck-recovery rung ended because an install drain began while the ladder held its instance.

recovery_ladder_drill_already_running.description: A drill of an instance's stuck-recovery ladder was refused because a ladder already holds or waits for the instance and recovery_ladder.rules.already_running is suppress (Workflow #390 DRILL-1). Its recovery_ladder_suppressed, tagged drill, says already_running.
recovery_ladder_drill_already_running.common_causes: A ladder a failure started, or an earlier drill, still holds or waits for the instance.
recovery_ladder_drill_already_running.handling: Wait until that ladder's recovery_ladder_finished, then ask again.

recovery_ladder_drill_cooling_down.description: A drill of an instance's stuck-recovery ladder was refused because the instance's cool-down window is open and recovery_ladder.trigger_defaults.respect_cooldown holds the drill (Workflow #390 DRILL-1). next_eligible_unix_ms is the window's end; its recovery_ladder_suppressed, tagged drill, says cooldown.
recovery_ladder_drill_cooling_down.common_causes: A ladder got the instance's key within the cool-down window (recovery_ladder.cooldown_secs or the instance's stuck_recovery_cooldown_secs), or a device drill did.
recovery_ladder_drill_cooling_down.handling: Ask again from next_eligible_unix_ms, or set recovery_ladder.trigger_defaults.respect_cooldown to false for the drill.

recovery_ladder_drill_disabled.description: A drill of an instance's stuck-recovery ladder was refused because stuck recovery is off for that instance, so no ladder starts on it (Workflow #390 DRILL-1). The command's command.rejected carries it; nothing else is recorded.
recovery_ladder_drill_disabled.common_causes: instances[].stuck_recovery or recovery_ladder.enabled is false for the instance.
recovery_ladder_drill_disabled.handling: Turn stuck recovery on for the instance (actingctl config set) if the drill should run, then ask again.

recovery_ladder_drill_queued.description: actingctl ladder-drill: the Runtime admitted a drill of the instance's stuck-recovery ladder and queued its claim; the line carries the drill {instance_alias, mode, ladder_request_id}, as ac_ladder_drill answers it (Workflow #390 DRILL-1).

recovery_ladder_drill_requested.description: The trigger of a drill's stuck-recovery ladder: a person asked for a drill of the instance's ladder (DrillRecoveryLadder, actingctl ladder-drill, MCP ac_ladder_drill; Workflow #390 DRILL-1). Its recovery_ladder_started names it as the trigger's failure_code with stage drill; every record of the drill's own is tagged drill.
recovery_ladder_drill_requested.common_causes: A person asked for a drill of the instance's ladder.
recovery_ladder_drill_requested.handling: Nothing to do; follow the drill's records by its ladder_request_id.

recovery_ladder_exhausted.description: A stuck-recovery ladder ran out of rungs after the rungs that ran failed on their own (or every rung was skipped); the recovery_ladder_finished record's outcome, caused by the last failed rung's outcome when one failed.

recovery_ladder_instance_missing.description: The Runtime host reports recovery ladder instance missing.

recovery_ladder_interrupted.description: A holding interruption (shutdown, a lost key, an install drain, a closed admission, a pause drain or a key renewal refusal) ended a stuck-recovery ladder's climb; the outcome of the recovery_ladder_finished record and of the recovery_rung_finished record of the rung it ended, caused by the interruption.

recovery_ladder_key_lost.description: A stuck-recovery ladder found, at a holding check, that it no longer holds its instance's key. It cancels its continuation, records the current rung failed with this reason and finishes exhausted at warning, without an error point.
recovery_ladder_key_lost.common_causes: In practice only a stopping host; otherwise a step that overran its own bound so the key lapsed.
recovery_ladder_key_lost.handling: Nothing to repair: the instance is handed on, and the next trigger starts a new ladder.

recovery_ladder_package_missing.description: The Runtime host reports recovery ladder package missing.

recovery_ladder_recovery_package_missing.description: The Runtime host reports recovery ladder recovery package missing.

recovery_ladder_shutdown_requested.description: A stuck-recovery rung ended because a Runtime shutdown was requested while the ladder held its instance.

recovery_ladder_startup_package_missing.description: The Runtime host reports recovery ladder startup package missing.

recovery_preparation_unconfirmed.description: The Runtime host reports recovery preparation unconfirmed.

recovery_readiness_adb_unconfirmed.description: The Runtime host reports recovery readiness adb unconfirmed.

recovery_rung_result_invalid.description: The Runtime host reports recovery rung result invalid.

recovery_rung_skipped_adb_unavailable.description: A stuck-recovery ladder skipped a rung because the instance's ADB baseline does not answer (the rung's recovery_rung_finished outcome; formerly the reason adb_unavailable).

recovery_rung_skipped_before_start_rung.description: A stuck-recovery ladder skipped a rung before the start rung its trigger item names (the rung's recovery_rung_finished outcome; Workflow #387 D1c, recovery_ladder.triggers[].start_rung or trigger_defaults.start_rung).
recovery_rung_skipped_before_start_rung.common_causes: A trigger item, or the trigger defaults, start the climb at a later rung.
recovery_rung_skipped_before_start_rung.handling: Nothing to do; change the trigger item's start_rung to climb from an earlier rung.

recovery_rung_skipped_capture_unavailabl.description: A stuck-recovery ladder skipped a rung because the instance's capture channel is known to be unavailable (the rung's recovery_rung_finished outcome; formerly the reason capture_unavailable).

recovery_rung_skipped_device_not_ready.description: A stuck-recovery ladder skipped a rung whose entry the device-state gate holds: a locked screen, heat, a low battery or a device in use (the rung's recovery_rung_finished outcome; skip reason device_not_ready, Workflow #398 M398 section 6.4, registered with Workflow #387 D1c; the device-state slice emits it).

recovery_rung_skipped_drill_plan.description: A plan drill of a stuck-recovery ladder did not run a rung the ladder would have run: a plan drill never acts on the device (the rung's recovery_rung_finished outcome; skip reason drill_plan, Workflow #390 DRILL-1). The climb ends planned.
recovery_rung_skipped_drill_plan.common_causes: A drill was asked for without --device (MCP device false).
recovery_rung_skipped_drill_plan.handling: Nothing to do. Ask for the drill with --device (device true) to climb the rungs on the device.

recovery_rung_skipped_input_unavailable.description: A stuck-recovery ladder skipped a rung because the instance's input channel is known to be unavailable (the rung's recovery_rung_finished outcome; formerly the reason input_unavailable).

recovery_rung_skipped_no_emulator_contro.description: A stuck-recovery ladder skipped its emulator_restart rung: the instance has no emulator control (the rung's recovery_rung_finished outcome; formerly the reason no_emulator_control).

recovery_rung_skipped_no_recovery_packag.description: A stuck-recovery ladder skipped its return_home rung: the failed run bound no recovery package and no return-home package is configured for its game and server (the rung's recovery_rung_finished outcome; formerly the reason no_recovery_package).

recovery_rung_skipped_no_startup_package.description: A stuck-recovery ladder skipped its application_restart rung: the instance has no startup package (the rung's recovery_rung_finished outcome; formerly the reason no_startup_package).

recovery_rung_skipped_resource_fence.description: A resource fence's stuck-recovery ladder skipped a rung that cannot prove the instance's close (the rung's recovery_rung_finished outcome; Workflow #403). The return-home rung only runs a package and never re-prepares the instance, so only the application restart and the emulator restart rungs can lift a fence.
recovery_rung_skipped_resource_fence.common_causes: An unconfirmed close fenced the instance and handed it to the ladder.

registry_entry_invalid.description: A MuMuPlayer uninstall registry entry carries no usable install location, or a value of a type the resolver does not read (install_source registry_uninstall). A MuMu resolution reason reaches outcomes where the refusing step runs: check-config's MuMu note (a note link of check_config_passed when the MuMu folder cannot be resolved), provider startup's device failure at a start, and the failure of a capture or input open in a running Runtime. The context the resolution recorded travels as optional values when the emitting path has it: count_kind, count and count_known (what was counted, how many, and whether the count is exact), install_source (which resolver rung chose the installation), configured_adb_class, explicit_root and explicit_dll (how the adb, the MuMu folder and the capture DLL were configured), and mumu_root.
registry_entry_invalid.common_causes: A damaged or partial uninstall entry left by an interrupted install or uninstall.
registry_entry_invalid.handling: Repair or reinstall MuMu, or set mumu_root to the installation folder.

registry_source_unavailable.description: The Windows uninstall registry, one rung of MuMu resolution, cannot be read on this platform (install_source registry_uninstall). A MuMu resolution reason reaches outcomes where the refusing step runs: check-config's MuMu note (a note link of check_config_passed when the MuMu folder cannot be resolved), provider startup's device failure at a start, and the failure of a capture or input open in a running Runtime. The context the resolution recorded travels as optional values when the emitting path has it: count_kind, count and count_known (what was counted, how many, and whether the count is exact), install_source (which resolver rung chose the installation), configured_adb_class, explicit_root and explicit_dll (how the adb, the MuMu folder and the capture DLL were configured), and mumu_root.
registry_source_unavailable.common_causes: A platform without the Windows registry, or registry access denied.
registry_source_unavailable.handling: Set mumu_root to the installation folder so the registry is not needed.

replay_facts_invalid.description: The --facts file of actinglab replay is not one complete instance fact answer of a Runtime: the result of actingctl facts --instance or of MCP ac_facts with scope instance (scope, read_at_unix_ms, snapshot, records_total, records_kept), read without key_prefix so that it holds every record, with a valid snapshot, within 4 MiB.
replay_facts_invalid.common_causes: The answer was read with --key-prefix, is of another scope, or was edited.
replay_facts_invalid.handling: Read the instance's facts again without a key prefix and save the answer unchanged.

replay_facts_unreadable.description: actinglab replay could not open or read the --facts file.
replay_facts_unreadable.common_causes: The path does not exist or is not readable.

replay_frames_invalid.description: The --frames directory of actinglab replay holds an entry that is not a PNG file (a subdirectory, a link or a file without the .png extension). Every entry of the directory is a frame, replayed in file-name order.
replay_frames_invalid.common_causes: Other files were saved beside the frames.
replay_frames_invalid.handling: Keep only the PNG frames in the directory.

replay_frames_unreadable.description: actinglab replay --frames could not list the --frames directory or one of its entries.
replay_frames_unreadable.common_causes: The path does not exist, is not a directory, or is not readable.
replay_frames_unreadable.handling: Name a readable directory of PNG frames.

replay_run_refused.description: actinglab replay --frames replayed the whole package over the frame sequence and the replayed run did not complete. The details carry the replay (entry check, steps, recognitions) and, as end.outcome, the outcome the run ended with; offline_fixture_exhausted when the run needed a frame after the last one of the sequence. Nothing was executed; the exit code is that of a usage refusal, so a CI job fails on it.
replay_run_refused.common_causes: The package no longer recognizes a recorded page or guard; the sequence ends before the run does; a select step chose nothing with the given facts.
replay_run_refused.handling: Read end.outcome and the last step of the details; fix the package or record a sequence that reaches the run's end.

replay_scan_invalid.description: The --scan file of actinglab replay is not one scan declaration of a select step (selector model S0 v2.1 section 2.1: every member, no unknown member), within 1 MiB.
replay_scan_invalid.common_causes: A member is missing, misspelt or of the wrong type, or the file holds more than the declaration.
replay_scan_invalid.handling: Save the step's scan declaration alone, with every member it requires.

replay_scan_refused.description: actinglab replay --frames --select --scan replayed the scan of the select step over the frame sequence through the kernel's scan path, and the scan did not cover its list. Either the selection evaluator ended it before its coverage (end.status aborted, end.coverage not_started or incomplete, the decision in scan.decision) or it failed (end.status failed, the outcome in end.outcome; selection_scan_replay_frame_missing when it needed a frame the sequence does not hold, such as a corrective, a rewind or a capture after the last frame). Nothing was executed; the exit code is that of a usage refusal, so a CI job fails on it.
replay_scan_refused.common_causes: The pack no longer finds or reads the recorded list; the recording is not a forward run from the list's start to its end; a declared fact list is missing from the given facts.
replay_scan_refused.handling: Read end and the scan's viewports in the details; fix the pack or the scan declaration, or record a forward run that reaches the list's end.

replay_scan_unreadable.description: actinglab replay could not open or read the --scan file.
replay_scan_unreadable.common_causes: The path does not exist or is not readable.

root_mismatch.description: A resolved backend file (the configured adb, the capture DLL or the folder of a running MuMu executable) belongs to another MuMu installation root than the one selected. A MuMu resolution reason reaches outcomes where the refusing step runs: check-config's MuMu note (a note link of check_config_passed when the MuMu folder cannot be resolved), provider startup's device failure at a start, and the failure of a capture or input open in a running Runtime. The context the resolution recorded travels as optional values when the emitting path has it: count_kind, count and count_known (what was counted, how many, and whether the count is exact), install_source (which resolver rung chose the installation), configured_adb_class, explicit_root and explicit_dll (how the adb, the MuMu folder and the capture DLL were configured), and mumu_root.
root_mismatch.common_causes: Two MuMu installations, with the adb or the DLL configured from one and the folder from the other.
root_mismatch.handling: Configure the adb, the capture DLL and mumu_root from the same MuMu installation.

A MuMu resolution reason reaches outcomes where the refusing step runs: check-config's MuMu note (a note link of check_config_passed when the MuMu folder cannot be resolved), provider startup's device failure at a start, and the failure of a capture or input open in a running Runtime. The context the resolution recorded travels as optional values when the emitting path has it: count_kind, count and count_known (what was counted, how many, and whether the count is exact), install_source (which resolver rung chose the installation), configured_adb_class, explicit_root and explicit_dll (how the adb, the MuMu folder and the capture DLL were configured), and mumu_root.

runtime_halted.description: The Runtime halted: a condition latched the host, which answers every later request without doing it. As a receipt's Runtime error code (runtime_code) it says the host is latched; a latched host answers with an error condition under runtime_halted as its caused_by link, and with a fatal condition as itself. A restart clears it.
runtime_halted.common_causes: A failure the host latches on, such as a lost ledger write or an internal invariant, and every request after it.
runtime_halted.handling: Read the caused_by link; restart the daemon (the watchdog restarts an error stop), and fix the condition first when it is external.

scrcpy_server_digest_mismatch.description: #402 RD-3: the scrcpy server the executable carries does not match the SHA-256 pinned in scripts/windows-tools/windows-tool-sources.v1.json, or the build embedded none; the scrcpy capture backend of the instance that opens it does not open, and the server is never pushed to the device. A damaged or incomplete installation. Only that instance's scrcpy capture backend is unavailable; the Runtime goes on (coordinator ruling 10-13, board #403 direction).

scrcpy_server_start_failed.description: #402 RD-3: the scrcpy capture backend could not start: pushing the server, the adb forward, starting the server, connecting to it, its stream header or its first frame failed within the start timeout. The open fails as capture_backend_open_failed. Only that instance's run fails and the recovery ladder handles it; the Runtime goes on (coordinator ruling 10-13, the instance-level rule of board #403).

scrcpy_stream_ended.description: #402 RD-3: the scrcpy video stream stopped: the server exited, the socket closed, a packet was malformed or H.264 decoding failed. No frame is delivered from a stream that ended; the capture fails instead of falling back to another backend. Only that instance's run fails and the recovery ladder handles it; the Runtime goes on (coordinator ruling 10-13, the instance-level rule of board #403).

scrcpy_video_size_mismatch.description: #402 RD-3: the scrcpy stream's video size is not the unscaled size requested (the display, or its centred crop to the size alignment), so its frames would be scaled; the stream is refused instead of downsampled. When it happens at the start, the open fails as capture_backend_open_failed. Only that instance's run fails and the recovery ladder handles it; the Runtime goes on (coordinator ruling 10-13 09:2x: every scrcpy code is instance-level).

selection_confirmation_capture_failed.description: A select step's confirmation frame could not be captured.

selection_empty.description: A selection decision chose nothing, which its document allows.

selection_evaluation_aborted.description: Retired. A scheduling-layer selection document met an unknown input under an abort_evaluation clause, and the whole scheduling evaluation failed for every instance. Since 0.12.0 the scheduling layer defers only the candidate that read the input (fact_refresh_unbound or selection_input_unknown) and the round goes on.
selection_evaluation_aborted.common_causes: An instance fact the document reads was missing or expired on one instance while the document declared abort_evaluation for it.
selection_evaluation_aborted.handling: None in 0.12.0 and later: the code is no longer emitted. Before 0.12.0, refresh the fact or change the clause to drop_candidate.

selection_evaluation_failed.description: A select step's selection policy evaluation failed.

selection_fact_context_mismatch.description: A select step's fact snapshot names another game or server than the package.

selection_input_unknown.description: A gate or term (rule_id) of a scheduling-layer selection document met an unknown input (unknown_reason) for a candidate on the instance that no reading can supply: an instruction key or pack data no instruction supplied, a fixed field, or a lookup that covers no value. Only that candidate is deferred, with no wake; it is evaluated again when the instance facts or the catalog change. One entry is written per rule that met such an input.
selection_input_unknown.common_causes: An instruction key (session.) was never set for the instance; the document's lookup lacks an entry and a default for a value the candidate has; the document reads a field the candidate does not carry.
selection_input_unknown.handling: Supply the instruction for the instance, or fix the selection document (add the lookup entry or default, or read a field the scheduling layer provides) and approve the catalog again.

selection_insufficient.description: Fewer selection candidates survived than the document requires; nothing is chosen.

selection_not_selected.description: A select step's selection policy selected no candidate.

selection_scan_alignment_rejected.description: A select step's scan session found no single shift for a frame: not exactly one consistent cluster of anchor pairs lay inside the window its motion admits (scan_alignment_failure says why; count is the pairs of the best cluster, limit_count the declared min_overlap_instances). Under page-order evidence (Workflow #308 SEL-L3b) the shift is the page: not exactly one declared page check passed, or the one page is neither the previous viewport's nor the next (no_consistent_shift, ambiguous_shift, unexpected_displacement; count is the page checks that passed, limit_count 1). The Runtime never guesses a second time.

selection_scan_bounds_exceeded.description: A select step's scan session ran out of a declared bound (scan_bound): its coverage viewports or its rewind and return viewports (limit_count), or its time (timeout_ms: max_ms, or the task's remaining time when shorter).

selection_scan_end_unconfirmed.description: A select step's scan session advanced twice without the list moving (two consecutive forward viewports repeated the one before them) and without the declared end check passing; the scan is stuck, and repeats never end a scan by themselves.

selection_scan_gap_detected.description: A select step's scan session left a gap in its coverage: after the one corrective reverse advance of that gap, a coverage band still started gap_px later than the union before it minus the instance extent allows; viewport_index names the corrective viewport.

selection_scan_identity_mismatch.description: A select step's scan session read a position with another Known identity (observed_identity) than the one it had read there before (expected_identity); position_index names the position and viewport_index the viewport of the later reading.

selection_scan_instance_missing.description: A select step's scan session found a missed anchor through a declared spacing check (scan_spacing_failure: a row gap, a short row, a leading, trailing or cross gap); gap_px is the distance found, or count and limit_count the positions of a row and the declared columns.

selection_scan_position_unread.description: A select step's scan session tracked a position that never entered the readable band of any coverage viewport, so the coverage cannot be complete; position_index names the first such position and viewport_index the viewport that first saw it.

selection_scan_replay_frame_missing.description: A scan dry run over a saved frame sequence needed a frame the sequence does not hold: a corrective or rewind move (stage), or a capture after its last frame. The dry run fails; it never passes without the frames.

selection_scan_settle_incomplete.description: A select step's scan session captured frames at the declared settle interval, and no two consecutive captures gave the same core anchor set before the settle timeout (timeout_ms) ended; viewport_index names the viewport being settled.

selection_scan_start_unconfirmed.description: A select step's scan session could not prove the start of its list: the declared start check failed on the settled first frame and the scan declares no rewind, or two consecutive rewind viewports repeated the one before them without the start check passing (stage select_scan_start). No selecting input was made.

selection_selected.description: A selection decision chose the required number of surviving candidates.

selection_state_unavailable.description: The runtime has no instance fact snapshot or instant for a select step.

selection_unknown.description: A selection evaluation ended unknown: a record list could not be read, or an unknown input reached a rule whose document ends the evaluation (unknown_reason).

selection_unknown_clause_ignored.description: A gate or term (rule_id) of a scheduling-layer selection document declares a drop_candidate or substitute clause (unknown_clause) that the scheduling layer does not apply: there an unknown input defers the candidate that read it. The document's author meant something else than what runs. An abort_evaluation clause gives no warning.
selection_unknown_clause_ignored.common_causes: A selection document written for an in-task select step, where the clauses apply, is used as the scheduling-layer document.
selection_unknown_clause_ignored.handling: Expect the candidate to be deferred instead of dropped or scored with the substitute; to keep the clause's effect, use the document in a select step instead.

session_feature_fact_invalid.description: A session.feature. record breaks the feature-lock fact rules (its value is not a boolean, or it declares invalidate_on events); the publication request is refused. Not fatal.
session_feature_fact_invalid.common_causes: A client wrote a number or a text, or attached invalidation events.
session_feature_fact_invalid.handling: Publish a boolean record without invalidate_on.

session_pack_schedule_invalid.description: A session.pack.schedule record breaks the pack schedule rules (field points at the offending member): its value is not a record_list of package_id, from_unix_ms, until_unix_ms and schedulable rows, a row ends at or before it starts, or two rows of one package overlap. The publication request is refused. Not fatal.
session_pack_schedule_invalid.common_causes: A client wrote overlapping periods for one package or swapped from and until.
session_pack_schedule_invalid.handling: Write the scope's whole list again with non-overlapping rows.

session_timeout.description: An agent session reached its deadline without a response: the Runtime answers it NeedsHuman with this code as the response code (formerly the unregistered spelling session_timeout).

sha256_invalid.description: The artifact store reports sha256 invalid.

shared_adb_multiple_dll_versions.description: The configured adb is MuMu's shared adb, and the installation holds more than one versioned Nemu capture DLL, so the version to pair with it is ambiguous (count_kind dll_versions, count the number found). A MuMu resolution reason reaches outcomes where the refusing step runs: check-config's MuMu note (a note link of check_config_passed when the MuMu folder cannot be resolved), provider startup's device failure at a start, and the failure of a capture or input open in a running Runtime. The context the resolution recorded travels as optional values when the emitting path has it: count_kind, count and count_known (what was counted, how many, and whether the count is exact), install_source (which resolver rung chose the installation), configured_adb_class, explicit_root and explicit_dll (how the adb, the MuMu folder and the capture DLL were configured), and mumu_root.
shared_adb_multiple_dll_versions.common_causes: A MuMu installation that keeps several emulator engine versions.
shared_adb_multiple_dll_versions.handling: Configure the capture DLL explicitly (device_paths.nemu_ipc_dll) or use the versioned adb of the engine in use.

shutdown_wait_journal_unreadable.description: actingctl's shutdown wait could not read the owner journal under the state root: path names the file, line the record that does not decode, and the decoder's or the OS error is the caused_by link. Exit 1.
shutdown_wait_journal_unreadable.common_causes: A journal written by another release, a damaged journal file, or a state root the process may not read.
shutdown_wait_journal_unreadable.handling: Check the state root the configuration names and its owner journal; run actingctl status to see the Runtime's state.

shutdown_wait_timeout.description: actingctl request-shutdown --wait or install-transition --wait: the accepted owner did not close and exit within timeout_ms. pid and owner_epoch name the owner; owner_closed and process_alive are what the wait last saw, and a failed process probe is the caused_by link. Exit 1.
shutdown_wait_timeout.common_causes: Work in flight that takes longer than the wait to drain, a Runtime that hangs while closing, or a wait set too short.
shutdown_wait_timeout.handling: Run actingctl status to see whether the Runtime still answers; wait longer, or check the Runtime's log for what holds it.

The Runtime records it at startup and refuses, in preparation, a run that needs the root; check-config lists it; the resource tools share the same check. A broken root never stops the Runtime.

start_emulator_requires_discovery_bindin.common_causes: start_emulator set on an explicit or fixture instance.
start_emulator_requires_discovery_bindin.handling: Bind the instance by instance_index or instance_name, or remove start_emulator. Fix the configuration and commit it again with acsetup --commit-config; run actingd check-config to confirm before restarting the daemon.

target_executable_missing.description: The running MuMu device process of the target has no readable executable path, so its installation cannot be derived (count_kind matched_target_processes, count 1). A MuMu resolution reason reaches outcomes where the refusing step runs: check-config's MuMu note (a note link of check_config_passed when the MuMu folder cannot be resolved), provider startup's device failure at a start, and the failure of a capture or input open in a running Runtime. The context the resolution recorded travels as optional values when the emitting path has it: count_kind, count and count_known (what was counted, how many, and whether the count is exact), install_source (which resolver rung chose the installation), configured_adb_class, explicit_root and explicit_dll (how the adb, the MuMu folder and the capture DLL were configured), and mumu_root.
target_executable_missing.common_causes: The process runs elevated or under another account, so its path cannot be read.
target_executable_missing.handling: Run the emulator and the Runtime as the same user and elevation, or set mumu_root.

target_identity_invalid.description: The target instance's explicit MuMu instance id is out of range. A MuMu resolution reason reaches outcomes where the refusing step runs: check-config's MuMu note (a note link of check_config_passed when the MuMu folder cannot be resolved), provider startup's device failure at a start, and the failure of a capture or input open in a running Runtime. The context the resolution recorded travels as optional values when the emitting path has it: count_kind, count and count_known (what was counted, how many, and whether the count is exact), install_source (which resolver rung chose the installation), configured_adb_class, explicit_root and explicit_dll (how the adb, the MuMu folder and the capture DLL were configured), and mumu_root.
target_identity_invalid.common_causes: A negative or too large instance id in the configuration.
target_identity_invalid.handling: Correct the instance's MuMu instance id or bind the instance by discovery.

target_identity_mismatch.description: The instance id the target's serial implies and the explicit MuMu instance id differ. A MuMu resolution reason reaches outcomes where the refusing step runs: check-config's MuMu note (a note link of check_config_passed when the MuMu folder cannot be resolved), provider startup's device failure at a start, and the failure of a capture or input open in a running Runtime. The context the resolution recorded travels as optional values when the emitting path has it: count_kind, count and count_known (what was counted, how many, and whether the count is exact), install_source (which resolver rung chose the installation), configured_adb_class, explicit_root and explicit_dll (how the adb, the MuMu folder and the capture DLL were configured), and mumu_root.
target_identity_mismatch.common_causes: An instance id kept after the instance's port changed, or a serial of another instance.
target_identity_mismatch.handling: Make the endpoint and the instance id name the same MuMu instance, or bind the instance by discovery.

target_identity_unavailable.description: No MuMu instance id can be derived for the target from its adb serial, and none is configured. A MuMu resolution reason reaches outcomes where the refusing step runs: check-config's MuMu note (a note link of check_config_passed when the MuMu folder cannot be resolved), provider startup's device failure at a start, and the failure of a capture or input open in a running Runtime. The context the resolution recorded travels as optional values when the emitting path has it: count_kind, count and count_known (what was counted, how many, and whether the count is exact), install_source (which resolver rung chose the installation), configured_adb_class, explicit_root and explicit_dll (how the adb, the MuMu folder and the capture DLL were configured), and mumu_root.
target_identity_unavailable.common_causes: An instance whose serial is not one of MuMu's local port serials, for example a handset or a renamed endpoint.
target_identity_unavailable.handling: Use the MuMu endpoint MuMu assigns to the instance, bind the instance by discovery, or choose another capture backend.

target_match_not_unique.description: A target that declares unique did not pass: a second place scores at least the best match's score minus margin_milli (Workflow #396 REC-2). For a template, a position whose box does not intersect the best match's and that meets the target's own acceptance condition; for a locate OCR target, another block whose text matches, its confidence counted as 0 when absent. Scores are in milli, rounded down. Carried as the target evaluation's failure; a guard refuses its input with it as the cause.

target_match_search_incomplete.description: The exact score map of a template target that declares unique (Workflow #396 REC-2) or mask (Workflow #396 REC-7) was not complete within the search limit timeout_ms. An evaluation error: the target never passes on a partial search.

target_process_absent.description: No running MuMu device process matches the target instance (count_kind matched_target_processes, count 0, install_source running_process). A MuMu resolution reason reaches outcomes where the refusing step runs: check-config's MuMu note (a note link of check_config_passed when the MuMu folder cannot be resolved), provider startup's device failure at a start, and the failure of a capture or input open in a running Runtime. The context the resolution recorded travels as optional values when the emitting path has it: count_kind, count and count_known (what was counted, how many, and whether the count is exact), install_source (which resolver rung chose the installation), configured_adb_class, explicit_root and explicit_dll (how the adb, the MuMu folder and the capture DLL were configured), and mumu_root.
target_process_absent.common_causes: The emulator instance is stopped, or it runs under another account.
target_process_absent.handling: Start the emulator instance, then retry.

target_process_ambiguous.description: More than one running MuMu device process matches the target instance (count_kind matched_target_processes, count a lower bound: count_known false). A MuMu resolution reason reaches outcomes where the refusing step runs: check-config's MuMu note (a note link of check_config_passed when the MuMu folder cannot be resolved), provider startup's device failure at a start, and the failure of a capture or input open in a running Runtime. The context the resolution recorded travels as optional values when the emitting path has it: count_kind, count and count_known (what was counted, how many, and whether the count is exact), install_source (which resolver rung chose the installation), configured_adb_class, explicit_root and explicit_dll (how the adb, the MuMu folder and the capture DLL were configured), and mumu_root.
target_process_ambiguous.common_causes: Several MuMu installations or engine versions running the same instance number.
target_process_ambiguous.handling: Stop the duplicate emulator processes, or set mumu_root to the installation to use.

An evaluation error.

An evaluation error.

timeout_invalid.description: A device instance's timeout (command_timeout_ms, handshake_timeout_ms, shutdown_timeout_ms or tap_hold_ms) is 0 or above its upper bound. check-config refuses at stage config_assemble; a start refuses before the ledger opens.
timeout_invalid.common_causes: A timeout written in seconds instead of milliseconds, or set to 0.
timeout_invalid.handling: Set the timeout in milliseconds within the bound, or remove it for the default. Fix the configuration and commit it again with acsetup --commit-config; run actingd check-config to confirm before restarting the daemon.

touch_backend_invalid.description: A device instance's touch_backend is missing or not a backend name the Runtime knows. check-config refuses at stage config_assemble; a start refuses before the ledger opens.
touch_backend_invalid.common_causes: touch_backend left out, or a typing error in its value.
touch_backend_invalid.handling: Set touch_backend to one of the documented backends. Fix the configuration and commit it again with acsetup --commit-config; run actingd check-config to confirm before restarting the daemon.

touch_backend_must_be_explicit.description: A device instance's touch_backend is an automatic choice (auto or auto_fastest), which the daemon does not accept. check-config refuses at stage config_assemble; a start refuses before the ledger opens.
touch_backend_must_be_explicit.common_causes: A configuration that relied on automatic touch selection.
touch_backend_must_be_explicit.handling: Name the touch backend explicitly. Fix the configuration and commit it again with acsetup --commit-config; run actingd check-config to confirm before restarting the daemon.

upgrade_state_aborted.description: The reply to an UpgradeState enter that was still waiting for the drain when an UpgradeState cancel withdrew the transition. The Runtime keeps running.
upgrade_state_aborted.common_causes: A second installer run or a script sent cancel during the drain.
upgrade_state_aborted.handling: Nothing to repair; enter the upgrade state again when the upgrade should go on.

upgrade_state_cancelled.description: UpgradeState cancel took effect while the transition was still draining: admission reopened, the transition is recorded as aborted and the Runtime keeps running.
upgrade_state_cancelled.common_causes: An interrupted installer run again, or a person or a script withdrew the upgrade.

upgrade_state_entered.description: UpgradeState enter succeeded (#389 U-4): the Runtime closed admission, drained, recorded its scheduling pause, accepted its own close while the requesting connection was still open, and closes with the upgrade-state marker on its owner-journal close record.
upgrade_state_entered.common_causes: acsetup entered the upgrade state before it replaces or restarts the Runtime.
upgrade_state_entered.handling: Nothing to repair. The installer goes on; if it fails after this point, the watchdog, when its task is registered, starts the selected generation again once the installer has released install\writer.lock.

upgrade_state_released.description: UpgradeState leave succeeded: the Runtime that acsetup started with --install-held prepared its provider, restored the pause recorded by the transition and opened admission.
upgrade_state_released.common_causes: acsetup released the Runtime it started held, after it checked the process id and the request id.

upgrade_state_requester_disconnected.description: The connection that sent UpgradeState enter closed before the Runtime accepted its own close. The Runtime handles it as cancel: admission reopens, the transition is recorded as aborted with this code as its failure_code, and the Runtime keeps running. No request receives this code as its reply.
upgrade_state_requester_disconnected.common_causes: The installer process ended or was killed while the Runtime was draining.
upgrade_state_requester_disconnected.handling: Run the installer again; the Runtime is unchanged and running.

usage_invalid.description: actingd was started without exactly --config <path> (or --config <path> --install-held <json>). The daemon line is a start refusal; exit 1.
usage_invalid.common_causes: A launcher or script that passes other arguments, an empty path, or an unknown subcommand name.
usage_invalid.handling: Start actingd as actingd --config <path to actingd.config.json>.

validation_failed.description: A code several owners emit with one meaning (contract-owned, A2a D3): validation failed.

value_test_not_met.description: A value test did not pass: both sides read, and the left value compared with the right one (a constant, or the other read value times mul plus add) does not satisfy value_op (Workflow #396 REC-6). target_id is the value test. Carried as the target evaluation's failure: a page whose rule needs the value test does not match, and a guard refuses its input with it as the cause. The values are not values of the code; they are in the value test's evidence.

value_test_unresolved.description: A value test did not pass because one of its sides could not be read (Workflow #396 REC-6). target_id is the value test; value_side names the side (the left side is reported first) and value_problem why: the trimmed text was empty, not in the declared format or too large for 64 bits, its value (or the declared part) lay outside min..=max, the OCR target's region could not be resolved, or the read's confidence was missing or below the OCR target's minimum_confidence. A provider failure is an evaluation error instead. Carried as the target evaluation's failure: a page whose rule needs the value test does not match, and a guard refuses its input with it as the cause. The read text and value are not values of the code; they are in the value test's evidence.

vendor_stdio_residue_facts_exceeded.description: Event or record sanitization refused a value: vendor stdio residue facts exceeded.

vendor_stdio_steps_exceeded.description: Event or record sanitization refused a value: vendor stdio steps exceeded.

version_mismatch.description: The adb (or the running MuMu executable) and the Nemu capture DLL carry different engine versions (nx_device/<version>); they must match. A MuMu resolution reason reaches outcomes where the refusing step runs: check-config's MuMu note (a note link of check_config_passed when the MuMu folder cannot be resolved), provider startup's device failure at a start, and the failure of a capture or input open in a running Runtime. The context the resolution recorded travels as optional values when the emitting path has it: count_kind, count and count_known (what was counted, how many, and whether the count is exact), install_source (which resolver rung chose the installation), configured_adb_class, explicit_root and explicit_dll (how the adb, the MuMu folder and the capture DLL were configured), and mumu_root.
version_mismatch.common_causes: A MuMu update that left an older adb or DLL configured, or files configured from two engine versions.
version_mismatch.handling: Configure the adb and the capture DLL of the same engine version, or remove the explicit paths to let the resolver pair them.

vision_config_invalid.description: The vision section breaks its rules: execution_provider cuda without a valid cuda_device, cpu with a cuda_device, or an empty root. check-config refuses at stage config_assemble; a start refuses before the ledger opens.
vision_config_invalid.common_causes: cuda_device left out for cuda, or kept after switching to cpu; root set to an empty string.
vision_config_invalid.handling: Name a cuda_device only with cuda, and give root a path or remove it. Fix the configuration and commit it again with acsetup --commit-config; run actingd check-config to confirm before restarting the daemon.

vision_model_folder_invalid.description: A vision root's model listing cannot be used: a model folder breaks the folder rule (check-config and vision-provider-check refuse it; startup records it). Startup records each such folder with its path and, when it fits the name rule, its model_name.

vision_models_empty.description: A vision root's model listing cannot be used: the models directory holds no model folder.

vision_provider_manifest_retired.description: actingd's configuration names the retired vision provider manifest, which the vision root replaced (Workflow #360). check-config refuses at stage config_assemble; a start refuses before the ledger opens.
vision_provider_manifest_retired.common_causes: A configuration written for a Runtime release before the vision root.
vision_provider_manifest_retired.handling: Remove the member and configure the vision section instead; commit the configuration again with acsetup --commit-config.

vision_provider_path_encoding_invalid.description: Provider startup refused a vision path (the root, a model or runtime file) that is not valid UTF-8 before recording it; the recorded failure is path_encoding_invalid. The start fails.
vision_provider_path_encoding_invalid.common_causes: A vision root under a folder whose name is not representable as UTF-8.
vision_provider_path_encoding_invalid.handling: Move the vision root to a folder with a plain name and set vision.root accordingly. Fix the configuration and commit it again with acsetup --commit-config; run actingd check-config to confirm before restarting the daemon.

vision_provider_unavailable.description: Provider startup could not build the vision provider from the models the vision root lists; the vision provider's refusal is the caused_by link (relayed). The start fails.
vision_provider_unavailable.common_causes: A model folder whose files the provider cannot use, or a runtime library that does not load.
vision_provider_unavailable.handling: Run actingd check-config to list the vision root, repair or remove the model folder, then start again.

vision_root_in_program_slot.description: The vision root resolves inside a program slot (A or B) of the install root, which the installer replaces on an upgrade. check-config refuses at stage config_vision; a start refuses before the ledger opens.
vision_root_in_program_slot.common_causes: vision.root pointing into <install root>\A or <install root>\B.
vision_root_in_program_slot.handling: Keep the vision root outside the slots (the default is <install root>\vision). Fix the configuration and commit it again with acsetup --commit-config; run actingd check-config to confirm before restarting the daemon.

vision_root_unavailable.description: A vision root's model listing cannot be used: the root or its models directory is unavailable. actingd's startup listing, its check-config and vision-provider-check refuse the root with it.

vision_runtime_unavailable.description: The vision root lacks a usable ONNX Runtime: ort\onnxruntime.dll, or for execution_provider cuda the CUDA provider library, is missing or cannot be read. The OS error, when there is one, is the caused_by link. check-config refuses at stage config_vision; a start refuses before the ledger opens.
vision_runtime_unavailable.common_causes: An incomplete vision root (the ort folder not copied), cuda configured with a CPU-only runtime, or files removed by antivirus.
vision_runtime_unavailable.handling: Restore the ort folder of the vision root (the installer places it), or switch execution_provider to cpu, then run actingd check-config again.
